name: Piltai
overview: Piltai was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Miniamin. He is noted among the priests, descendants of Aaron, emphasizing his role within the Levitical priesthood. His mention in Nehemiah 12:17 situates him within the post-exilic community serving in religious duties.
namesAndTitles: The name Piltai means 'Y-H-V-H rescues,' reflecting a theologically rich name that acknowledges God's saving power. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:17, highlights the believer's trust in the Lord's deliverance, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Piltai was the son of Miniamin, as noted in Nehemiah 12:17. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Piltai's significance lies in his inclusion among the Levitical priests, descendants of Aaron, during the period of restoration after the exile. His lineage and priestly role underscore the continuity of God's covenantal priesthood in Israel. Through individuals like Piltai, the faith community maintained its worship and dedication to the Lord in accordance with divine ordinances.
